original_hook: When $ONE pulled back 16% from its $0.001898 peak, hourly volume collapsed by over 75%—dropping from 2.71B tokens during the surge to 346M tokens on the retreat. That steep volume contraction signals short-term profit-taking rather than institutional distribution. Because liquidity was swept clean during the advance, overhead ask depth remains thin. The bullish consolidation holds as long as price sits above local support at $0.001515. Confirmation for a secondary expansion requires a 1H close above $0.001707 on volume expanding back over 800M tokens. Conversely, a high-volume hourly close below $0.001515 invalidates the flag and risks a retracement to $0.00125. 📊 ONE 1H: price $0.001579 • support $0.00067 • resistance $0.001898 • TP1 $0.002205 • target $0.002512 • SL / invalidation $0.00067 (long bias). Levels are chart-derived scenarios, not guarantees. What confirmation on $ONE would make you treat this setup as real rather than an early headline move?
